summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent pulmonary emboli on warfarin, diverticulosis, dementia, and chronic chest wall pain was admitted for chest and abdominal pain, diarrhea, dizziness, and severe anemia. She was found to have a hemoglobin of 6.5 g/dL, no evidence of active gastrointestinal bleeding on CT or guaiac testing, and a urinary tract infection confirmed by urinalysis. She received one unit of packed red blood cells with improvement in hemoglobin to 8.0 g/dL and was treated with IV ceftriaxone, later transitioned to oral Bactrim for a 10-day course. Her chest pain was determined to be non-cardiac, likely due to costochondritis and cervical spine issues, and she remained hemodynamically stable throughout. Warfarin was adjusted due to drug interaction with Bactrim. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up on INR, complete antibiotics, and consult a hematologist for ongoing anemia management.
